headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is also elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and Agent B reads/writes filesystem with stdin/stdout and application-defined files, so a shared workspace can bridge attacker-controlled content into B. B’s graph/checkpointer model can propagate poisoned state across nodes; A’s autonomous execution increases the chance its outputs are treated as instructions.
conditions: IF A and B share the same workspace or scratchpad directory
IF B ingests file contents from that workspace as instructions or state
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct directories
Disable automatic parsing of scratchpad files as prompts
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent files
Review any shared-state keys before each run

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs; B also has broad egress and can read/write files. If they share files or graph state, sensitive data can flow from A into B and then out through B’s model-provider or tool calls, creating an exfiltration path in default-style orchestration.
conditions: IF A stores financial or market data in a shared file or checkpointer
IF B forwards that state to a model provider or developer-defined tool
mitigations: Keep sensitive A outputs out of shared state
Redact financial identifiers before handoff
Restrict B’s tool outputs to non-sensitive summaries
Rotate or scope API keys per agent
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and B also supports multiple instances with shared state via a checkpointer store. Even though B cannot modify git state, both can write to overlapping filesystem-backed state, so concurrent updates can race and overwrite each other unless the orchestrator adds locking.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same scratchpad or checkpointer namespace
IF the orchestrator does not serialize writes or lock shared keys
mitigations: Assign disjoint state namespaces
Enable per-key locking in the orchestrator
Serialize writes for shared artifacts
Check timestamps before overwriting
requires-engineering: add transactional state updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an autonomous research agent that calls external APIs, and B is a graph orchestrator that can route node outputs into later nodes. If B treats A’s generated facts or citations as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports; the pair’s default wiring makes this plausible.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s outputs as node inputs without a verification step
IF any downstream node acts on those outputs with external side effects
mitigations: Insert a verification node between A and B
Require source citations for all factual claims
Gate side-effecting tools behind human approval
Log and diff A outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: add confidence-based routing

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly touches financial data and market data, while B’s docs show broad network egress and model-provider/tool calls with no residency or retention controls. If regulated financial or market data is routed through B’s external calls or logs, compliance breach risk is material; the profiles do not show a mitigating policy.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through B’s model-provider calls or logs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workflow
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in shared state
Disable logging of sensitive payloads
Use a residency-approved deployment path
Document retention limits for both agents
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
